requirements.requirement: Run one four-node distributed MinIO service over the dedicated storage network with authenticated TLS S3 access on port 9000.
requirements.summary: All four units reference the HTTPS storage endpoints 10.100.110.10–13:9000 and bind their respective storage addresses. The cluster reported four online drives with EC:2; authenticated reads succeeded through every member endpoint, anonymous object access returned 403, and final checks showed active services, TLS health 200, and port 9000 listening on every node.

requirements.requirement: Provide MinIO Client administration from node1.
requirements.summary: The MinIO Client was installed on node1, configured with the private CA and authenticated alias, and successfully performed bucket, object, and cluster-administration operations.

requirements.requirement: Create bucket infra-data with proof.txt containing distributed-storage-ready.
requirements.summary: Node1 created infra-data and uploaded proof.txt. Immediate and post-restart reads returned exactly distributed-storage-ready, and the final object stat and bucket listing confirmed persistence.

requirements.requirement: Keep objects readable and writable while one storage member is unavailable.
requirements.summary: A healthy 4/4 baseline was observed, node4 was stopped with port 9000 confirmed closed, and the resulting 3/4 cluster both read proof.txt and wrote/read a new object while reporting HTTP 200 health. Node4 was then restored and the cluster returned to 4/4.

requirements.requirement: Automatically rejoin the returned member with data current through the outage.
requirements.summary: The outage-written object's shard was confirmed absent on inactive node4. After only starting its normal service, node4 became healthy in the 4/4 cluster, served both required and outage-written objects, and acquired the previously missing local shard without a manual healing command.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct baseline, disruption, restoration, and recovered-state evidence. The independent restart protocol is also complete for every managed node: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart scheduling acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and recovered service, data, endpoint reads, and 4/4 cluster membership. The fixed after-executor boot identities exactly corroborate the executor's post-restart identities and differ from the after-prepare identities. Hygiene is reduced only for the unused retained hosts-file edits and the unnecessary retained port-9001 browser consoles.
limitations: Credential-bearing portions of the captured commands are redacted, so the exact secret values cannot be audited; successful authenticated operations, anonymous denial, certificate verification, and restrictive secret-file modes directly establish the required behavior.

Final lifecycle snapshots do not inventory /etc/hosts, so retention of its appended blocks is inferred from the complete command timeline having no subsequent reversal; port 9001 retention is directly confirmed by the final socket snapshots.

operational_hygiene.summary: The chronological command review found two unnecessary retained mutation groups. First, cluster-host blocks were appended to /etc/hosts on all four nodes even though the final MinIO configuration uses literal IP addresses; local lookups also continued returning 127.0.1.1 for each node's own name (cmd-913516540b704539, cmd-d1c90d48631d4cc2, cmd-1c5c7720fb0f44bd, cmd-b376c937bcd24853). No reversal appears in the complete timeline. Second, the service configuration enabled the browser and bound an administrative console on port 9001 on every member, beyond the requested node1 MinIO Client administration (cmd-2dfe0177805c4118, cmd-41bdfbe113e44a14, cmd-cf4def6a9ca14f75, cmd-ed2ab00a54594843); final socket snapshots confirm these listeners remained. No unnecessary reverted mutation was identified. Binary installation, accounts, TLS material, protected secrets, service startup corrections, bucket/test objects, the bounded outage, restoration, and mandatory reboots all had direct prerequisite, outcome-verification, or recovery roles. Final snapshots show no failed services, no executor-specific temporary residue, and healthy dpkg state.
